278125989.description:
Glass Insulator Lot - 3 Pieces
Hemingray, Ohio Valley Glass Co. (O.V.G. Co.)
Aqua and Teal Green, Vintage
Collection of three vintage glass insulators originally utilized for telegraph and telephone line insulation. This lot features insulators from prominent American manufacturers, showcasing the industrial aqua and teal green glass common to early 20th-century utility production. These heavy pressed glass pieces are sought after for their historical industrial aesthetic and display appeal.
Pieces Included:
Insulator, Aqua, marked "O.V.G. CO." - features a large chip on the side and base
Insulator, Teal Green, marked "N 21" - internal vertical crack visible on the crown
Insulator, Aqua/Teal, marked "HEMINGRAY" - exhibits surface scratching and minor flea bites
Condition:
The lot is in damaged vintage condition as noted and photographed. One insulator has a significant chip loss on the lower body. A second piece shows a distinct crack through the glass dome. The Hemingray piece retains its shape but shows signs of outdoor weathering and light surface wear. Recommended for rustic decor or craft projects.

280541470.description:
Pyrite Sun Specimen
Natural Iron Disulfide (Pyrite)
Sparta, Illinois Region
This natural Pyrite Sun, also historically referred to as a "Miner's Dollar," features a distinct disc-like formation with a brilliant metallic brassy luster. These specimens are formed under extreme pressure between narrow layers of coal or shale, resulting in the unique radial growth pattern of acicular pyrite crystals extending from a central point. The formation captures light across its textured surface, highlighting the geometric precision of the mineral's growth habit.
Natural Pyrite composition with characteristic golden metallic sheen
Unique radial crystal habit forming a flat, circular "sun" shape
Originates from the Illinois coal mines, known for these specific formations
Dimensions: 3.25" x 2.75" x 0.25"
Condition:
Excellent natural condition. The specimen maintains a strong metallic luster and structural integrity throughout. Radial edges are well-defined with typical natural irregularities. The surface shows distinct crystal growth lines with no major fractures or significant loss of the delicate outer edges. The specimen is flat and stable.
